# **Architecture Blueprint: Autonomous Development Driven by AI Agents (V3)**

This document serves as the comprehensive, exhaustive, and operational reference guide for implementing a fully automated software engineering pipeline driven by AI agents (specifically within environments like Google Antigravity coupled with the Conductor orchestration extension). It covers the entire lifecycle from initial scoping by the Product Owner to autonomous production deployment, eliminating functional blind spots, isolating architecture, optimizing data strategies, validating implementations, and strictly controlling token consumption.

## **1\. Context, Origins & Overall Philosophy**

### **1.1 The origin: Conductor & Google Antigravity**

This methodology relies on the same philosophy as **Conductor, BMAD, Spec-Kit**, orchestration extensions (to integrate into the **Google Antigravity** harness). It enables spec-driven development (*Spec-Driven Development*) by coordinating autonomous AI agents from structured specification documents, managing task breakdown, code generation, documentation automation, and continuous verification of requirements.

### **1.2 Separation of Human Scoping & Autonomous Execution**

The core philosophy of this metholodogy rests on a clear boundary:

> * **Supervised Scoping Phase (Human / PO in the loop):** The human defines the vision, validates the 360° PRD, arbitrates the upstream architecture decision matrix (docs/architecture.md), and approves the initial task breakdown.   
>   This represents 99% of the heavy lifting : making sure the PRD and architecture is comprehensive enough for the automated loop to converge to a satisfying state.  
> * **Fully Autonomous Loop Execution Phase (Background Agents):** Once rules and contracts are sealed, the orchestrator executes the development loop (detailed specification, adversarial review, test writing, coding, E2E validation, merge) without interrupting the user, except on critical exceptions (*Interrupt Hooks*).

## **2\. Exhaustive Upstream Scoping & Product Owner (PO) Assistance**

To eliminate the *"garbage in, garbage out"* risk (where an incomplete PRD leads to agent hallucinations or regressions), the upstream phase is locked down by two specialized skills and a 360° completeness grid.

### **2.1 Skill /interview-prd (Guided Scoping & Augmented Recommendations)**

When the PO initiates a major project or complex feature, this agent conducts a structured interactive interview. If the PO lacks a technical answer or hesitates on an engineering decision, the agent activates its **augmented recommendation mode powered by web research/state-of-the-art analysis**:

> * **Comparative Analysis:** The agent researches current market best practices and formulates 2 to 3 concrete proposals.  
> * **Synthetic Decision Matrix:** It presents a detailed comparison table (Pros / Cons / Estimated Financial Cost / Maintenance Complexity / Performance).  
> * **Validation & Inscription:** As soon as the PO decides, the agent records the choice directly into the specification dossier.

### **2.2 360° Completeness Grid (The 6 Mandatory Pillars)**

A PRD document cannot be approved for autonomous development unless it fully satisfies the requirements of all six pillars below:

| 360° Pillar | Requirements & Mandatory Elements to Specify   |
| :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Functional Vision** | Target personas, critical user journeys (happy paths), business edge cases, handling user input errors, business cancellation/rollback rules. |
| **2\. Stack & Architecture** | Frontend/backend frameworks, API typing and protocols (REST, GraphQL, gRPC), application state management, allowed third-party dependencies and libraries. |
| **3\. Data Strategy** | Entity and relationship modeling, persistence engines (SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redis), estimated volume and growth, backup policy, schema migration strategy. |
| **4\. Infra & Deployment** | Hosting target (SaaS, public cloud such as GCP, Bare-metal, Docker/Podman containerization, self-hosted server), environments (Dev, Staging, Prod), CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure budget caps. |
| **5\. Security & Compliance** | Authentication engine (OAuth, JWT, Passkeys), role-based access control (RBAC), encryption at rest and in transit, GDPR compliance, privacy management, and protection of living individuals' data. |
| **6\. Non-Functional & UX** | Target SLAs and response times, responsive design, overall UI/UX design, offline/degraded connectivity behavior, internationalization (i18n), accessibility (a11y). |

### **2.3 Skill /audit-prd (The Inflexible Gatekeeper)**

This skill acts as a strict completeness linter:

> 1. It audits the docs/PRD.md document against the 360° Grid.  
> 2. If any mandatory section is missing, ambiguous, or incomplete, it **technically blocks** access to downstream commands (/arch-gate and /implementation-loop).  
> 3. It presents the PO with a series of targeted questions or multiple-choice prompts to resolve missing items in a single interactive iteration, then seals the PRD.

## **3\. Upstream Architecture Decision Gate Phase (/arch-gate)**

Positioned between the validated PRD and backlog generation, the /arch-gate skill extracts all architectural variables from the PRD (e.g., choice of DBMS, local vs. GCP hosting, authentication provider). It submits a single decision matrix to the human. The validated choices are recorded in the immutable document docs/architecture.md, which all sub-agents refer to in order to prevent unauthorized stack changes.

## **4\. Code Methodological Foundations (The Tryptych \+ Type-Safety)**

### **4.1 Spec-Driven Development (SDD — Macro Level)**

SDD governs the breakdown of the global PRD into atomic issues (/prd2backlog) and then into detailed task specifications (/specify). No line of code is generated without a clear spec defining inputs, outputs, and business invariants in advance.

### **4.2 Functional Core / Imperative Shell (FC / IS — Architectural Isolation)**

Inspired by traditional software engineering (hexagonal architecture, formalized by Gary Bernhardt over 10 years ago), this pattern strictly separates pure logic from side effects:

> * **Functional Core (src/core/):** Contains 100% of pure business logic (calculations, rules, validations). It is pure, deterministic code with no I/O, no network calls, and no SQL. For AI, this core guarantees maximum reliability. It can be executed and tested in milliseconds without containers or complex mocks. If the Web framework or database changes, the Core remains entirely untouched.  
> * **Imperative Shell (src/shell/):** Technical plumbing wrapping the business core. The Shell handles HTTP requests, retrieves data from DBs, injects them into the Core for processing, and applies side effects (SQL writes, email sending, UI rendering). This prevents agents from tangling business rules with infrastructure.

### **4.3 Contract-First & Type-Driven Development**

Before writing any Core or Shell code, the agent produces strict data schemas (Zod, Pydantic, OpenAPI, or TypeScript interfaces). These interface contracts lock data exchanges between the technical wrapper and the core, prohibiting the agent from inventing implicit properties during coding.

### **4.4 Test-Driven Development (TDD — Micro Level)**

Code writing discipline at the micro level (*Red → Green → Refactor*). The agent first writes the failing unit test, writes the minimum required code to pass it, and then refactors. Test success serves as a factual, deterministic stopping criterion for the agent.

## **5\. Validation, Testing & Data Strategies**

### **5.1 E2E Integration via Browser Agent**

Once the application is compiled and running, Antigravity's browser agent (running headless Playwright) opens the browser, simulates real user clicks, fills out forms, verifies visual and DOM rendering, and confirms the validation of end-to-end user journeys before submitting work.

### **5.2 Eval-Driven Development (EDD — Embedded AI Agent Testing)**

EDD activates **exclusively if the final application integrates an embedded AI sub-agent or LLM** (e.g., a historical/genealogical research chatbot). EDD is completely inactive for a standard application without AI.

> * **Dataset of Goldens (Reference Dataset):** Construction of a reference conversation dataset containing ideal question/answer pairs based on ground truth (e.g., *"Where was the great-grandfather born in 1912?"*).  
> * **Relevance Measurement & Non-Regression:** EDD automatically evaluates the probabilistic behavior of the embedded model at each iteration to measure answer precision, block hallucinations, and detect reasoning drift over time.

### **5.3 Data Strategy: Architectural Selection Matrix for AI-Database Integration**

Integrating an AI agent with an application's persistence layer requires a surgical approach to avoid the dual traps of **unnecessary Vector RAG over-engineering** and **context window flooding**. Directly injecting massive datasets leads to prohibitive latency, exploding token costs, and catastrophic model distraction.

The selection of a data architecture pattern must be strictly governed by the **underlying data structure**, the **total volume**, and the **semantic nature of queries**:

#### **5.3.1 The Three AI Data Integration Patterns**

**A. Direct Context Injection (Full Context)**

> * **Use Case:** Static reference datasets or small lookup tables (typically under \~20k tokens).  
> * **Mechanism:** The raw dataset is embedded directly within the system prompt.  
> * **Strategic Trade-off:** Offers immediate implementation but fails to scale, incurring recurring token consumption on every interaction.

**B. Tool Calling & Text-to-SQL (Deterministic Structured Querying)**

> * **Use Case:** Structured or relational databases (SQLite, PostgreSQL) requiring absolute precision and complex joins.  
> * **Mechanism:** Only the *database schema* is injected. The agent generates a targeted **SELECT** query and executes it via a read-only tool.  
> * **Strategic Trade-off:** Zero vectorization overhead, minimal token usage, and total elimination of hallucinations regarding relational data.

**C. Vector Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Vector RAG)**

> * **Use Case:** Unstructured corpora, such as PDFs or massive knowledge bases, requiring semantic similarity search.  
> * **Mechanism:** Employs chunking, embedding pipelines, and vector similarity retrieval.  
> * **Strategic Trade-off:** Significant setup complexity; inherently unsuitable for exact counting or precise relational operations.

---

#### **5.3.2 Pattern Selection Matrix**

| Data Nature | Dataset Size | Pattern | Advantage |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Small Reference** | \< 20k tokens | Direct Context | Minimal Infra. |
| **Structured DB** | Any scale | Text-to-SQL | Deterministic accuracy. |
| **Unstructured** | Growing corpora | Vector RAG | Semantic search. |

---

#### **5.3.3 Essential Data Security & Safety Guardrails**

Independently of the selected pattern, the following infrastructure-level safety protocols must remain immutable:

> * **Read-Only Sandboxing:** All AI-driven database interactions must utilize restricted accounts, strictly prohibiting destructive commands (*DROP, DELETE, UPDATE*).  
> * **Data Privacy & PII Redaction:** Implementing automated role-based sanitization of sensitive personal data before query results reach the agent.  
> * **Grounding & Anti-Fabulation Protocols:** System prompts must compel the agent to explicitly refuse answers if the retrieval layer provides no factual evidence.

## **6\. Loop Engineering (/implementation-loop), Sub-Agents & Interrupt Hooks**

### **6.1 Sub-Agent "Spec Reviewer" (Adversarial Multi-Agent)**

A classic issue with TDD executed by a single agent is its tendency to modify the test to pass it rather than fixing its code. To eliminate this bias, an independent sub-agent (*Reviewer*) operates within the loop: it audits specs and code diffs against the PRD and docs/architecture.md. If the spec or code is non-compliant, it rejects the proposal and requests a fix from the drafting agent transparently without human intervention.

### **6.2 Sequence of the Autonomous /implementation-loop**

The orchestrator executes the autonomous loop issue by issue following the chain:

/specify → /review-spec → /tdd-build (Core/Shell) → /e2e-test → /ship

### **6.3 Interrupt Hooks (Programmed Exception Pauses)**

The agent pauses the \`/implementation-loop\` and alerts the user only in three specific scenarios:

> 1. Detection of a missing secret, API key, or environment variable.  
> 2. Exceeding the maximum number of test fix attempts (Circuit Breaker).  
> 3. Irreconcilable architectural conflict with the docs/architecture.md file.

## **7\. Token Optimization & Quota Management**

| Optimization Technique | Description & Practical Implementation   |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Model Cascading** | Task allocation guided by [Google AI Latest Models Documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/latest-model): high-throughput, cost-effective models (e.g. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite) for spec review, formatting, JSON parsing, issue creation, and log cleaning. Advanced reasoning models (e.g. Gemini 3.6 Flash) reserved for architecture design, complex TDD, and stubborn debugging. |
| **Stateless Sub-Agents** | Full context window reset (Context Reset) at the start of each sub-task. The agent receives only 3 elements: architecture.md, the current issue spec, and the specific source files directly modified. Avoids costly history accumulation. |
| **Log Trimming** | Scripted local filtering of terminal outputs. Upon test failure, the script strips node\_modules stack traces and injects only the exact assertion message, source file name, and offending line number into the LLM prompt. |
| **Diff Patching** | Absolute prohibition against regenerating multi-hundred-line files for minor changes. Obligation to output targeted diff/patch blocks. |
| **Circuit Breakers** | Hard iteration cap enforced by the orchestrator (e.g., maximum 3 automated fix attempts per test). Beyond that, pause, save project state, and hand control back to human. |

## **8\. Project Structure & Governance**

my-project/  
├── AGENTS.md                  \# Project constitution (FC/IS rules, model cascades, circuit breakers)  
├── .agent/  
│   └── skills/                \# Specialized executable skills  
│       ├── interview-prd.md   \# /interview-prd (PO Scoping & Augmented Recommendations)  
│       ├── audit-prd.md       \# /audit-prd (360° Completeness Linter & Gatekeeper)  
│       ├── arch-gate.md       \# /arch-gate (Architecture Decision Matrix)  
│       ├── prd2backlog.md     \# /prd2backlog (Issue Backlog Generation)  
│       ├── specify.md         \# /specify (Detailed Spec Drafting)  
│       ├── review-spec.md     \# /review-spec (Adversarial Review Sub-Agent)  
│       ├── tdd-build.md       \# /tdd-build (TDD Cycle \+ Functional Core / Imperative Shell)  
│       ├── e2e-test.md        \# /e2e-test (Playwright Browser Agent Validation)  
│       └── ship.md            \# /ship (Main Merge and Commit)  
├── docs/                      \# Reference documents & state  
│   ├── PRD.md                 \# Validated PRD (100% 360° completeness)  
│   ├── architecture.md        \# Infrastructure decisions from /arch-gate  
│   └── specs/                 \# Specs per issue (e.g., issue-01.md)  
└── src/                       \# Application source code  
    ├── core/                  \# Functional Core (Pure deterministic code, 0 side effects, src/core/)  
    └── shell/                 \# Imperative Shell (I/O, SQL DB, HTTP API, UI, src/shell/)

**The Role of AGENTS.md:** This file serves as the supreme "Constitution" of the project. It compels all agents and sub-agents to adhere to Core/Shell isolation rules, mandatory TDD test writing, Model Cascading routing, log filtering, and Circuit Breaker execution limits.

### **9.2 Sequential Table of Interactive and Automated Commands**

| Sequence | Command / Skill | Mode | Action & Output Produced   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Step 1 | /interview-prd | Interactive (PO) | PO Interview, web research-augmented suggestions, initial drafting of docs/PRD.md. |
| Step 2 | /audit-prd | Automated (Gatekeeper) | 360° completeness audit, locking PRD at 100% or submitting resolution quizzes. |
| Step 3 | /arch-gate | Interactive (Human) | Single arbitration of infrastructure choices (DB, hosting, auth) → Generation of docs/architecture.md. |
| Step 4 | /prd2backlog | Automated | PRD breakdown into issue sub-specs in docs/specs/issue-\*.md. |
| Step 5 | /implementation-loop | Autonomous (Background) | Launch of autonomous loop: /specify → /review-spec → /tdd-build → /e2e-test → /ship. |
